verdict.rationale: Clerky's docs describe customizable questionnaire-driven document generation ('easy to customize the key terms') and attorney-review workflows ('loop in your attorney to have them review and comment on the information you're entering'), plus attorney oversight controls and full change logs. However, there's no explicit evidence of the questionnaire proactively flagging specific choices as needing attorney review (vs. just enabling manual invite-to-review), and no independent/hands-on confirmation of questionnaire accuracy or flagging logic. missing for 10: concrete evidence of automated flagging of risky/ambiguous answers, hands-on user account of the questionnaire flow itself, independent validation of legal correctness.
